newsitem.title: UK: Copper drifts in LME pre-market after probing high.
newsitem.headline: Copper drifts in LME pre-market after probing high.

text.p: Base metals prices tickled the upside in early pre-market trading on Friday, then drifted off the highs amid profit-taking and a lack of follow-through.
Zinc, which had powered up to 4-1/2 year highs on Thursday, again attracted a smattering of fund interest on Friday morning and traded as high as $1,338, traders said.
It subsequently eased back slightly to $1,331/$1,333, compared to the previous kerb close of $1,330.
Still, traders and analysts said zinc probably had further to go in the near term.
"Everyone's watching to see what funds do today in zinc. There seems to be plenty of scope to try $1,350," a trader said.
The other metals, however, prompted less bullish near-term forecasts.
Copper was also firmer initially, reaching $2,395 before profit-taking turned it lower to $2,386, off $2 from Thursday's kerb close.
"Copper saw some fund buying yesterday which helped it along. But $2,400 is a tough level and it's encountering forward selling," a trader said.
The cash to threes backwardation which had been underpinning the market also narrowed slightly to $56/$61, compared to $60/$65 at the close.
LME stocks, however, were up just slightly by 425 tonnes in line with expectations that inventory deliveries would slow down by the end of this week.
Flaring nearby spreads last week had attracted metal to LME warehouses, but the backwardation has since eased from highs of $210.
Aluminium was similarly looking toppy, failing early on just above the $1,670 level where it finished on Thursday.
Traders said it was likely to meander around current levels at $1,662 in the near term, with profit-taking limited advances for now.
The other metals were generally steady to easier, including lead which saw an LME stocks rise of 2,800 tonnes.
"There was some spec and fund buying in lead yesterday in sympathy with zinc. But the fundamentals don't justify it going any higher and it's unlikely to get much more of a boost," a trader noted.
Lead was last indicated at $633/$635, versus $636.
Tin was slightly lower at $5,870, compared to $5,910, while nickel was $70 easier at $7,770.
A breach of $7,800 resistance would target the $8,000 level, analysts said.
Alloy was indicated little changed at $1,500/10.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
